title: 2024 HMMT February Geometry Problem 9
statement: Let \(A B C\) be a triangle. Let \(X\) be the point on side \(\overline{A B}\) such that \(\angle B X C=60^{\circ}\). Let \(P\) be the point on segment \(\overline{C X}\) such that \(B P \perp A C\). Given that \(A B=6, A C=7\), and \(B P=4\), compute \(C P\).

solutions.text:
Construct parallelogram \(B P C Q\). We have \(C Q=4, \angle A C Q=90^{\circ}\), and \(\angle A B Q=120^{\circ}\). Thus, \(A Q=\sqrt{A C^{2}+C Q^{2}}=\sqrt{65}\), so if \(x=C P=B Q\), then by Law of Cosine, \(x^{2}+6 x+6^{2}=65\). Solving this gives the answer \(x=\sqrt{38}-3\).
